title: Order Evidence Collection by Volatility
prompt: Put the evidence sources in collection order, from most volatile to most stable.

items.label: Volatile memory (RAM): keys, payloads, and processes — capture before any shutdown
Active network connections, sockets, ARP table, and process state
Caches, buffers, and logs not yet written to disk
Persistent data on disk: files, registry, logs, bit-by-bit image
Backups, archives, and offline storage — least volatile

explain: The rule is to capture what disappears fastest first. A reboot destroys RAM, connections, and caches; disk and backups remain accessible longer, but must also be protected with hashing and chain of custody.
